name: Pale Green-Blue Grey
lede: Pale Green-Blue Grey is a very pale, nearly colorless grey with the faintest blue-green lean, one of Ridgway's 1912 systematic names, later picked up by the ISCC-NBS system.

sections.title: A systematic grey
sections.body:
The name comes from Ridgway's 1912 color standards, plate XLVIII, hue 45'''', tone f, read from a scan of an aged printed plate [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system lists the same area as block 185 under "bluish white," about 3.3 units from this exact shade [1]. Its Munsell notation, N 7.1, marks it as a true neutral: no hue at all, only a value step [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[sage-grey]], [[pale-payne-s-grey]], [[pale-violet-plumbeous]] and [[pearl]], at 2.9, 3.6, 4.4 and 4.7 ΔE [1]. Nothing in the dictionaries we hold explains why this particular step earned its own name, so that part is undocumented here [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, this grey appears in 475, about 2.0 percent, more common than 77 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 38 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.7 times the expected rate for that century, and inside a painting it is most often a light rather than a shadow [2].

[[painter:camille-pissarro|Camille Pissarro]] is its most devoted painter, present in 7 of his 50 works here, 5.5 times his museums' baseline [2]. The earliest match is a 1315 panel by Lippo di Benivieni, nearly six centuries before Ridgway's name, so that early hit is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a trace of this named grey, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[light-greyish-olive]] and [[linen-grey]] [2].
